content: In Cuba, a Catador (plural: Catadores) is a professional cigar taster or tester. Within cigar factories, these individuals play a critical role in quality control by evaluating a random selection of cigars produced by each Torcedor (cigar roller). This ensures that every week, the work of each Torcedor undergoes blind testing to maintain consistent quality standards. A Catador smokes only a small portion of each cigar and evaluates it based on a detailed scoring system. The scoring criteria include the following aspects: Appearance and construction Aroma Burn Draw Consistency Strength Flavour Overall quality During a single testing session, a Catador typically evaluates between three and five cigars. To cleanse their palate and avoid interference with the tasting process, they only consume unsweetened black tea between cigars. The majority of these testing sessions are conducted exclusively in the mornings to ensure optimal sensory acuity.
